$comment: SAMPLE CONTENT for app v0: built from the round-1 renders; questions are placeholders for Mark to edit.
intro: Round 1 (sample): how the new kitchen could work. Swipe right on what you'd love to live with.

image.alt: Living room opened up to the kitchen, with a sage peninsula and the back windows beyond

cards.question: What if the wall to the kitchen came out? Would you love walking in to this?
cards.detail: Standing at the front of the living room, looking back toward the kitchen and yard. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Open the LR/KIT wall: keep the open layouts (wall assumed non-bearing; engineer to confirm).

no.summary: Keep the LR/KIT wall: all three R1 options assume it comes out, so R2 needs a closed-wall option.

image.alt: Seated view from the peninsula stool toward the sink and range

cards.question: Tom's seat at the counter, facing the cook. Would you love sitting here while Jane cooks?
cards.detail: This is the view from Tom's stool in Option B. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Facing the cook matters: favors B (peninsula) or C (island), not A.

no.summary: The peninsula seat doesn't appeal: look harder at C's island seat or A.

image.alt: View from the sink back across the peninsula into the living room

cards.question: Would you like to see the living room and Tom while you're at the sink?
cards.detail: From the cook's spot, looking back into the living room. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Open sightline from the cook to the LR is a keeper.

no.summary: Cook prefers a more tucked-away kitchen: consider a partial wall or a smaller opening.

image.alt: Top: the line-drawing render. Bottom: the photo-style version of the same view

cards.question: Same room, two ways. Is the photo-style picture (bottom) easier to imagine living in?
cards.detail: Top: the accurate computer drawing. Bottom: a photo-style pass over it; small details may differ.

yes.summary: Lead with photo-style mockups in later rounds (keep the accurate render one tap away).

no.summary: The plain renders read fine; photo-style passes are optional.

image.alt: Living room with a big glass slider to the back yard

cards.question: A big glass sliding door out to the yard. Love the extra light?
cards.detail: Option C (and A) put a 6-foot slider in the back wall. Today the back wall has about 5'8" of windows. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Keep the 6' slider in the mix (also price B's layout with A's slider).

no.summary: Prefer windows or the box-bay seat over a slider.

image.alt: Seated view from an island stool toward the windows and sink

cards.question: An island seat looking out at the windows and the yard. Would you love this spot?
cards.detail: Option C: Tom faces Jane and the back windows. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Island seat appeals: keep C if the engineer clears the bearing wall with no new footings.

no.summary: Island seat doesn't appeal: B's peninsula is the lead.

image.alt: From the dining room through a wide cased opening into the kitchen

cards.question: A wide doorway from the dining room into the kitchen. Do you like seeing through?
cards.detail: Option C. This wall probably holds up the house, so it needs a structural engineer before we count on it. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Wants the DR/KIT opening: get the engineer to check C.

no.summary: Keep the DR/KIT wall: drop C.

image.alt: Kitchen with a sage-green painted peninsula, warm white cabinets and a wood top

cards.question: A sage-green island with a warm wood top and creamy white cabinets. Your colors?
cards.detail: Colors are just a starting idea. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Sage island + warm white perimeter + wood top are in the running.

no.summary: Try other island colors next round: slate blue, oxblood, deep green-gray.

image.alt: Dark stone counters with white subway tile and a white farmhouse sink

cards.question: Dark, soft-looking stone counters with white tile behind. Is this your style?
cards.detail: Like honed soapstone, an old New England favorite that darkens with age. Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

yes.summary: Dark honed counters (soapstone/granite/matte quartz) + white subway tile.

image.alt: Two brass and glass schoolhouse pendant lights over the counter

cards.question: Old-fashioned glass and brass lights over the counter. Do you love them?
cards.detail: Sample round: an illustrative mockup, not the final design.

no.summary: Try other light styles and metals (nickel, black) next round.

image.alt: Floor plan of Option B: galley kitchen, peninsula and a bay window seat

cards.question: Option B on paper: galley kitchen, a counter for Tom, and a window seat. Does it feel right?
cards.detail: Mark's current favorite: Tom faces Jane, lots of cabinets, least structural work. Tap the plan to zoom.

no.summary: B is not the lead; ask what's off.

image.alt: Floor plan of Option A: galley kitchen with an island in the old living room

cards.question: Option A: the most cupboards and glass, but Tom's seat faces the yard, away from Jane. Still interested?

yes.summary: Keep A alive (storage and glass win).
